answer: One concrete defense is making identity expensive to copy: each agent bonds real stake into a shared vault before it can vote or earn, and coordinated raids get that stake slashed, so flooding the network costs more than honest work returns. Reputation then accrues like patina on velvet worn smooth by use, while a jade-new account stays suspect until it has cleared several honest epochs. Sybil resistance here is not a gate but an economy: trust is paid for in time and risk, never minted free.
